name: Thousand Pillar Temple
description: Located at the base of Hanamkonda hill, the Thousand Pillar Temple is a premier example of Kakatiya architecture, featuring a magnificent Trikutalayam layout and a massive monolithic Nandi sculpture.
history: Built in 1163 AD by the Kakatiya King Rudra Deva, the temple stands as a testament to the architectural brilliance of the Kakatiya dynasty. It is currently preserved and maintained as a protected monument by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

sub_temples.name: Lord Shiva Shrine (Sri Rudreshwara Swamy)
sub_temples.description: Primary sanctum sanctorum of the Trikutalayam.

sub_temples.name: Lord Vishnu Shrine
sub_temples.description: Second sanctum of the Trikutalayam complex.

sub_temples.name: Lord Surya Shrine
sub_temples.description: Third sanctum of the Trikutalayam complex dedicated to the Sun God.

religious_significance: The temple is dedicated primarily to Lord Shiva and also houses shrines of Lord Vishnu and Lord Surya. Since it has three sanctums, it is known as Trikutalayam.
architectural_significance: The temple is famous for its beautifully carved pillars, monolithic Nandi statue, rock-cut elephants and intricate stone engravings representing Kakatiya craftsmanship.

architecture.nandi: A massive sculpture of Nandi, carved out of a single rock, is another attraction of this temple
architecture.rock_cut_elephants: Rock cut elephants and exquisite engravings at the temple are also worth noticing
architecture.architecture_description: Constructed using the stellar layout style, the temple features three shrines oriented around a central pillared hall (Natya Mandapam) supported by richly sculpted pillars and delicate rock-cut elements.
